comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C3-C5, C94. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers evaluate the theoretical framework as SUPPORTED, describing it as logically consistent, novel, and building on established principles. Peer reviewers call it a 'strong novel contribution' while OpenEval notes it is 'theoretically sound.'

Strong agreement on claims C6-C9, C95-C99. Both evaluate simulation results as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on specific simulation outcomes (synergistic epistasis, frequency distributions) while peer reviewers affirm simulations show 'the scenario works at least under some conditions.' Peer result R2 also includes C100-C101 which OpenEval addresses separately in R3.

Both address simulation results with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval R3 specifically covers claims C100-C101 about de novo emergence and crossover rate dependence, which peer reviewers include in their broader affirmation of simulation plausibility in R2.

Perfect agreement on claims C102-C109. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the mechanistic explanation for 0.25/0.75 frequencies and Hardy-Weinberg deviations, while peer reviewers note the 'analogies with sex chromosome evolution hypotheses' but also mention one prediction about 'nearly homozygously lethal haplotypes' may not reflect reality.

Perfect agreement on claims C110-C113. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the emergence of three equilibrium states and acknowledges uncertainty about barriers between states. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the theoretical framework demonstrating model complexity.

Major disagreement on claims C10-C11, C129-C130. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED based on experimental data and statistical testing, while peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, expressing 'significant reservations' about experimental design, noting it only addresses 'one element' of the hypothesis and that the design is 'not ideal.'

Major disagreement on claims C12-C13, C132-C133. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED based on sex-specific survival differences, while peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, questioning the relevance of 'survival until old age' to fitness under natural conditions and expressing concerns about experimental design.

Agreement on claims C138-C139. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the genomic data supports the model's prediction about disadvantageous doubly-inverted karyotypes. Peer reviewers accept this observation without direct critique as consistent with antagonistic interactions.

Partial overlap on claims C117-C118, C121. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED despite noting contradiction with specific predictions. Peer result R7 evaluates as UNCERTAIN and includes additional claims (C122-C125, C128), questioning experimental design and noting potential sampling bias and inability to explain clinal variation patterns.

Agreement on claims C136-C137 but different evaluation types. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting evidence is strongest for some inversions with important caveats. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the evidence is 'incomplete and tentative' and the paper is 'stronger as a theoretical than empirical contribution.'

Disagreement on claim C14 (and peer adds C72, C77). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, stating the combined evidence supports the model despite generality questions. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, noting 'the key problem is that the proposed model does not explain the patterns of clinal variation' observed in D. melanogaster.

Agreement on claims C126-C127 but different evaluation types. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting maternal genotype dependence as important biological complexity. Peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the experiment 'does not test for two other key elements' including frequency-dependence and synergistic epistasis.

Partial overlap on claims C122-C125. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting consistency of survival effects across maternal genotypes. Peer result R7 evaluates as UNCERTAIN and includes additional claims (C117-C118, C121, C128), expressing broader concerns about experimental design and model's ability to explain observed patterns.

Minimal overlap on claim C128. OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, noting departures from null expectations suggest selection is operating. Peer result R7 evaluates as UNCERTAIN and includes many additional claims (C117-C118, C121-C125), questioning the experimental design's ability to test the hypothesis.

OpenEval evaluates claims C168-C176 about sex chromosome evolution as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis is 'largely speculative' with limited empirical support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found that specifically addresses these claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C131, C134 as SUPPORTED, noting patterns for In(2L)t and In(2R)NS are consistent but weaker than other inversions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these claims.

OpenEval evaluates claim C135 as SUPPORTED, noting inversions do not strongly affect development time under experimental conditions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this negative result.

OpenEval evaluates claim C156 as SUPPORTED, noting the model generalizes to other antagonistic tradeoffs beyond the specific case studied. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this generalization.
